claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by initiating the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start with the first key question:

**How old is the child you're claiming for?**

Please tell me:
1. The child's name
2. The child's date of birth (or their current age)

This will help me determine which rules apply to them. Child Benefit has different eligibility criteria depending on the child's age.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 17 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about your son **Alex, who is 17 years old**.

Since Alex is in the 16-19 age range, I need to check whether he meets the education or training requirements. Let me get the details I need:

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or approved training?**

For Child Benefit purposes, 16-19 year olds can qualify if they're:
- In full-time education (like school, college, or university)
- In approved training (like an apprenticeship)

Can you let me know what Alex's current situation is?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. He finished school and hasn't started anything else yet.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. So Alex has finished school but isn't currently in education or training.

Let me navigate to the next step based on this information.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. Since Alex isn't currently in education or training, I need to check if he recently left education and might be eligible for an extension period.

**When did Alex finish school?** 

Specifically, was it:
- Within the last 20 weeks, or
- More than 20 weeks ago?

This matters because there's a specific extension period after leaving education where Child Benefit may still be payable.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It was more than 20 weeks ago. He's been out of school for quite a while now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Since Alex finished school more than 20 weeks ago and isn't currently in education or training, let me navigate to the outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that based on the information you've provided, **you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Here's why:**

Child Benefit is only payable for children who are:
- **Under 16 years old**, OR
- **Aged 16-19 and in approved full-time education or training**

Since Alex is 17, he would need to be in full-time education or approved training to qualify. Because he finished school more than 20 weeks ago and isn't currently in education or training, he no longer qualifies.

**Important note:** There is a transitional provision where if a 16-17 year old leaves education, Child Benefit can continue for up to 20 weeks if they register with a careers service or the armed services. However, as Alex left school more than 20 weeks ago, this period has passed.

**Next steps:**
- If Alex does start education or approved training in the future, you may be able to claim Child Benefit again from that point
- You can contact HMRC if you have any questions or if circumstances change

Is there anything else I can help clarify, or do you have any other children you'd like me to check eligibility for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, that's all I needed to know. Thank you for explaining it to me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're welcome! I'm glad I could help explain the situation clearly. 

If circumstances change for Alex in the future—for example, if he starts education or training—feel free to come back and we can reassess his eligibility.

Best of luck to Alex with whatever comes next, and thank you for using this service!
